land.text: Málaga, where Yahya I al-Mu'tali, the Hammudid caliph at Córdoba until 1026, returned and declared independence

predecessors.note: Hammudid Córdoba collapsed in 1026; Cliopatria has no Málaga row, its Caliphate of Córdoba shapes run to 1071.

land.text: Málaga, conquered by Granada in 1239 (1238 in the page text)

successors.note: The state existed in four periods (1026-1056/7, 1073-1090, 1145-1153, 1229-1239); in the gaps Málaga belonged to taifa-of-granada, almoravid-dynasty and almohad-caliphate, as the ledger records.

capitals.name: Málaga
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Málaga. Held only in the four periods the ledger gives.

rulers.name: Yahya I al-Mu'tali
rulers.note: Page: 1026 or 1027 to 1035. Hammudid caliph at Córdoba 1021-1023 and briefly 1025-1026.

rulers.name: Yahya III al-Mahdi
rulers.note: Page: 1054/5 to 1057/8; the Zirids took Málaga in 1056 (Taifa of Granada page) or 1057 (this page).

rulers.name: Tamim ben Buluggin
rulers.note: Zirid prince of Granada's ruling house, governor of Málaga.

rulers.name: Abu'l-Hakam al-Husayn
rulers.note: Died by suicide at the Almohad conquest in 1153.

rulers.name: Ibn Zannun
rulers.note: Page: 1229? to 1239; his fall is 1238 in the page text.

correction.text: Málaga, the capital of the new taifa; the page names no boundary

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row. The page gives the capital (Málaga) and says Yahya I 'united Málaga and Algeciras (the coras)' without a year; the Algeciras page dates the annexation 1035. No infobox area to compare.

correction.text: Málaga with Algeciras: 'Yahya al-Mu'tali annexed Algeciras to the taifa of Málaga in 1035'

keyframe_review.note: Algeciras is independent again from 1039. The Málaga page instead says the 1035 succession divided the kingdom into Málaga (Idris I) and Algeciras (Muhammad ben al-Qasim); the Algeciras page, which dates the annexation, is followed.

correction.text: Málaga alone after Algeciras reverted to Muhammad ibn al-Qasim in 1039

keyframe_review.note: 1039-1055 under the Hammudid claimants; the page names no boundary change.

correction.text: Málaga under Tamim ben Buluggin, Badis's grandson, 1073-1090

keyframe_review.note: Second period. Tamim attacked his brother Abd Allah of Granada's lands in 1081-82 (Taifa of Granada page) without a change of border being recorded.

correction.text: Málaga under Abu'l-Hakam al-Husayn, who exploited a revolt against the Almoravids
Málaga under Ibn Zannun, independent in 1229 until his fall in 1238/1239

ledger.note: 1026: Yahya I al-Mu'tali, the Hammudid claimant to the caliphate of Córdoba, returns to Málaga and declares it an independent taifa. 'The taifa was created in 1026 when' he returned and declared independence; Hammudid page: 'Ruled Taifa of Málaga afterwards (1026)'. The page gives the city, not a boundary, so the province is the reading.

1035: Yahya I annexes Algeciras to Málaga. 'Yahya al-Mu'tali annexed Algeciras to the taifa of Málaga in 1035.' The Málaga page says Yahya 'united Málaga and Algeciras' and 'conquered the Taifa of Carmona' (retaken by Seville) without years; Carmona is left out for want of a date.

1039: Algeciras is Muhammad ibn al-Qasim's again. 'In 1039 Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, son of al-Qasim, was proclaimed emir of Algeciras' (page does not say how Málaga lost it); in the same year 'Malagan victory at the Battle of Écija' (Málaga page).

region.text: Málaga, annexed by Badis of Granada after Hammudid rule collapsed

ledger.note: 1056: the Zirids annex Málaga. 'Badis nonetheless annexed Málaga in 1056 after Hammudid rule collapsed there.' The Málaga page (conquered 1057 by Badis ben Habus) and the Hammudid page (1056 in the text, 1057 in the table) disagree by a year; the Taifa of Granada page is followed so that the counterpart's gain matches. The Hammudids withdrew to Ceuta.

region.text: Málaga, passed to Tamim ben Buluggin when Badis died

ledger.note: 1073: Badis dies and Málaga 'went to Tamim ben Buluggin ben Badis', a separate Zirid taifa from Granada under Abd Allah (Tamim 1073-1090 in the succession table).

1090: the Almoravids conquer Málaga. 'In 1090, the taifa was conquered by the Islamic Almoravid dynasty' (Almoravid rule 1090-1145 in the table); the Taifa of Granada page has Granada itself taken in September 1090, the Málaga page gives no month.
1145: Málaga breaks from the Almoravids. Abu'l-Hakam al-Husayn ruled 1145-1153 'exploiting a revolt against the Almoravids' (second taifas period); the year is the succession table's.
1153: the Almohads take Málaga; Abu'l-Hakam kills himself (Almohad rule 1153-1229 in the table).
1229: Málaga 'became shortly independent in 1229' under Ibn Zannun as Almohad rule collapsed.

region.text: Málaga, conquered by the Emirate of Granada

ledger.note: 1239: Granada conquers Málaga. Infobox 'Conquered by Granada: 1239'; the page text says his fall in 1238 marked the end of the taifa.

region.text: Málaga, passed to the Emirate of Granada

ledger.note: 1239: the Taifa of Málaga ends; the land passes to Granada, which Cliopatria's Emirate of Granada row (from 1241) continues.

wars.name: Battle of Écija (1039)
wars.outcome: A Malagan victory on the Málaga page, a Zirid victory over the Abbadids of Seville near Écija on the Granada page; neither page names ground that changed hands.
wars.note: No territorial result recorded on either page.

wars.name: Zirid annexation of Málaga
wars.outcome: Badis of Granada annexed Málaga after Hammudid rule collapsed; the Hammudids fell back on Ceuta.

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of the taifas
wars.outcome: Granada fell in September 1090 (Taifa of Granada page) and Málaga to the Almoravids in the same year (Málaga page).

certainty.note: The pages name cities and no boundaries; every extent is a reading of the province or a radius around a town. The gaps (1056-1072, 1090-1144, 1153-1228) are years in which the land belonged to other states.

sources.title: Hammudid dynasty
sources.note: Caliphate at Córdoba 1016-1027, Málaga from 1026, the Zirid conquest 1056/1057, the retreat to Ceuta; Tangier, Ronda and Archidona are not on it.

sources.title: Taifa of Granada
sources.note: Badis annexed Málaga in 1056; Tamim and Abd Allah; the Almoravids took Granada in September 1090.

sources.title: Taifa of Algeciras
sources.note: Algeciras annexed to Málaga in 1035; independent emir 1039.

notes: Written for eu-12-x (states Cliopatria lacks); four pages. Cliopatria has no Málaga row; the Taifa of Málaga is one state in four periods, so the ledger records the gaps as losses to the Zirids (1056), the Almoravids (1090) and the Almohads (1153) and as gains from them in 1073, 1145 and 1229. Disagreements: Zirid conquest 1056 (Granada page, Hammudid text) or 1057 (Málaga page, Hammudid table, followed by neither here); end 1238 (text) or 1239 (infobox); the 1035 succession as annexation of Algeciras (Algeciras page) or as a division (Málaga page); Algeciras taifa 1035-1058 (lead) or 1013-1058. Not settled: the Málaga page says Yahya conquered Carmona and that Seville retook it, with no years; Ceuta and Tangier are not Málaga's on any page opened (the Hammudid page gives Ceuta to Ali and Algeciras, Tangier, Arzila to al-Qasim in 1013 or so, and 'Taifa kings of Ceuta 1009-1055'). Gazetteer: all names resolve through Natural Earth (Málaga province, a radius around Algeciras). Rulers are the page's table; reign overlaps (Muhammad I ben al-Qasim 1047-1053) are the page's own.
